verdict.rationale: Supermemory's first-party docs show the full loop. Developers send raw conversations to the add API and Supermemory extracts memories. They can create memories directly, which are 'embedded and immediately searchable'. Later they retrieve them with client.search, scoped by containerTag, with a recommended hybrid search mode, and customId supports incrementally updating ongoing conversations. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of recall quality, and explicit documentation of cross-session persistence beyond the implied durable containerTag scoping.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add memories from conversations and retrieve them later with semantic search, so context persists across sessions

citations.quote: Send any raw content to Supermemory — conversations, documents, files, URLs. We extract the memories automatically.
Memories are embedded and immediately searchable.
const results = await client.search({ q: "where does Alex work?", containerTag: "user_123", include: { relatedMemories: true }, });
Use `searchMode: "hybrid"` for best results. It searches both memories and document chunks, returning the most relevant content.
Use customId to update existing documents or conversations. When you send content with the same customId, Supermemory intelligently processes only what's new.
